REPORT_FORMAT_REFERENCE
# Academic insight report format

Use this hierarchy as a report contract, not as a fixed section count. Omit a subsection only when it has no evidence, and name the resulting coverage limit in the methodology.

## Opening pages

1. Title, technology scope, publication window, and report date.
2. Research scope: sources, inclusion rules, publication-status policy, and evidence limitations.
3. Executive insight: the central change in the field, the strongest supporting signals, and the main uncertainty.
4. Direction map: a compact table of research layers, directions, and current concerns.

## Each research direction

1. Direction title expressed as a change, tension, or research question.
2. Direction overview explaining why the problem matters.
3. Current concerns presented as two to four evidence-backed themes.
4. Representative work with title, authors, venue or repository, date, publication status, and stable link.
5. Core mechanism. Include a figure only when its source and caption can be verified.
6. Key result. Report numerical comparisons only from inspected full text, tables, or figures and retain metric conditions.
7. Direction judgment separating observed evidence from synthesis.
8. Engineering or application implication when it follows from the evidence and serves the requested audience.

## Synthesis and references

1. Cross-direction synthesis: shared state, dependencies, contradictions, and emerging system structure.
2. Open problems and evidence gaps.
3. Conclusion answering the research questions without introducing new claims.
4. Numbered bibliography with complete titles and stable DOI, proceedings, repository, or publisher links.

Use clear tables for direction maps and comparable experimental results. Do not force incomparable metrics, datasets, or evaluation settings into one ranking.

All "answered" decisions are proposals, not semantic review. Synthetic materials cannot establish real research findings.

Synthesis category is consensus|trend|comparison|disagreement|research_gap|limitation.
Question indexes are zero-based in Brief order, exactly once each. answered needs statements and null reason;
partial needs statements and a non-empty reason; unanswered needs no statements and a non-empty reason.
Include required sections in this order: executive_summary, scope_and_method, technology_overview, cross_paper_analysis, key_findings, limitations, research_gaps, references, evidence_appendix.
scope_and_method, references and evidence_appendix are host-rendered: empty statementIndexes and null missingReason.
For every other section, statementIndexes and missingReason are mutually exclusive. Non-empty statementIndexes require
missingReason:null; empty statementIndexes require an explicit non-empty missingReason. Never provide both. This rule also
applies to limitations and research_gaps. Indexes refer to statements, not evidence.
Every statement must be used by a section or question; do not duplicate text to inflate length. Always disclose limitations.
Describe gaps in THIS RUN in limitations, questionAnswers.reason or sections.missingReason, not as unsupported synthesis statements.
For limitations or research_gaps sections without supported conclusions, use empty statementIndexes and an explicit missingReason.
Background references alone never support a statement; do not relabel background evidence as supports to satisfy the format.
directions is required in new outputs. Group by the approved problems and mechanisms, not arbitrary keyword similarity.
Cover every approved question with at least one direction; use at most 12 coherent directions.
Use only existing statementIndexes for overview, themes, mechanism, keyResults, judgment and implications.
Do not put uncited factual claims in direction, layer or theme labels; labels are organizational descriptions.
Every component uses the same mutually exclusive statementIndexes/missingReason rule as a non-host section.
Provide two to four non-empty evidence-backed themes when available. With zero or one theme, give themeLimit;
with two to four themes, themeLimit must be null. Do not invent extra themes merely to fill the layout.
For numerical comparisons set keyResults.quantitative:true and cite only supporting fulltext evidence, retaining
metric, dataset and experimental conditions. Abstract-only qualitative results use quantitative:false.
Separate source_statement observations from synthesis judgments; implications require evidence and serve the target audience.
Cross-direction synthesis and conclusion reuse section paragraphs; they cannot introduce new uncited claims.
No verified image/caption is supplied in this input, so omit mechanism figures and disclose the limit.
REPORT_FORMAT_REFERENCE
# Academic insight report format

Use this hierarchy as a report contract, not as a fixed section count. Omit a subsection only when it has no evidence, and name the resulting coverage limit in the methodology.

## Opening pages

1. Title, technology scope, publication window, and report date.
2. Research scope: sources, inclusion rules, publication-status policy, and evidence limitations.
3. Executive insight: the central change in the field, the strongest supporting signals, and the main uncertainty.
4. Direction map: a compact table of research layers, directions, and current concerns.

## Each research direction

1. Direction title expressed as a change, tension, or research question.
2. Direction overview explaining why the problem matters.
3. Current concerns presented as two to four evidence-backed themes.
4. Representative work with title, authors, venue or repository, date, publication status, and stable link.
5. Core mechanism. Include a figure only when its source and caption can be verified.
6. Key result. Report numerical comparisons only from inspected full text, tables, or figures and retain metric conditions.
7. Direction judgment separating observed evidence from synthesis.
8. Engineering or application implication when it follows from the evidence and serves the requested audience.

## Synthesis and references

1. Cross-direction synthesis: shared state, dependencies, contradictions, and emerging system structure.
2. Open problems and evidence gaps.
3. Conclusion answering the research questions without introducing new claims.
4. Numbered bibliography with complete titles and stable DOI, proceedings, repository, or publisher links.

Use clear tables for direction maps and comparable experimental results. Do not force incomparable metrics, datasets, or evaluation settings into one ranking.

All "answered" decisions are proposals, not semantic review. Synthetic materials cannot establish real research findings.
